entries.note: Round 7 look, same asserted behaviour. Read on Round 7’s owners — TimedWorkoutFlow (src/ui/timed-workout-flow.tsx) with its one “Log results” action and LoggingOverlay drawn inside the flow, and TimedResultLog (src/ui/timed-result-log.tsx) inside it — through local helpers (the build’s src/test/timed-log-dialog.ts locators, `[data-timed-log-opener]` and `dialog.clr-accepted-log`, are the build’s and unused here). Round 7 opens each log as its attempt ends; the case closes it and opens it from the card’s action, so open, close and reopen are read as the build read them. The focused-dialog read is as in the keyboard case (head; the X read as the build read it, framed with `clr-hit` and inside `.clr-bleed`; R7-3 retirement; Round 7’s Save log). Round 7’s accepted gallery states are the route’s own TimedWorkoutFlow over the gallery’s block, run past its cap by the state’s own drive (`?state=<id>&open=1`) or finished by its own controls; Round 7 seeds no sample entries (the build’s `data-gallery-amrap="early"` and `data-gallery-race` variants do not exist), so the entries are typed over memory and read back as typed, never the plan’s. The amrap state reads a blank count tapped to 1, where the build’s seeded state read 3 tapped to 4.
